The first people to orbit the Moon in 50 years, coming home
NASA's lunar crew made it back after 683,000 miles. Here is the moment they hit the ocean.
How the Orion capsule looked hitting the Pacific after a 10-day Moon mission
caption:
NASA's Artemis II mission sent four astronauts further from Earth than any human since 1972. Over 10 days they flew around the Moon and back, covering more than 683,000 miles aboard the most advanced crewed spacecraft ever built.

The splashdown in the Pacific was the first time a crew-rated capsule came home from lunar distance in over 50 years. The footage was so striking that NASA replayed it multiple times in their own recap.

This is what it looks like when people come home from the Moon.
